goal_descriptions.grip: Cornering grip racing: fast laps with the tyres near their peak.
goal_descriptions.drift: Sliding: starting, holding and linking drifts at big angles.
goal_descriptions.highway: Wangan runs: top speed and calm handling at very high speed.
goal_descriptions.launch: Getting off the line with the least wheelspin and bog.
goal_descriptions.stability: Not spinning, handling bumps, landings and braking calmly.

params.label: Engine drag (fixed part)
params.desc: The engine fights itself with this much torque whenever you are not on full throttle. It is part of "friction = F1 + F2 x rpm", taken away as friction x (1 - throttle). Higher makes the revs drop faster when you lift and gives more engine braking.
params.risk: None found; very high values just kill the revs off-throttle.

goals.drift: Up: lifting slows the rear wheels more, helping to start a drift. Down: lifting keeps the wheels spinning, holding a drift smoother.
goals.stability: Up: more engine braking calms the car when you lift. Down: lifting off does almost nothing.

params.label: Engine drag (per rpm)
params.desc: Extra engine friction that grows with rpm (N·m for every rpm). At 5000 rpm the RX-7 value 0.07 gives 350 N·m of drag when you lift. Higher means much stronger engine braking at high revs and faster rev drop between shifts.

goals.drift: Up: big engine braking on lift can snap the rear out. Down: smooth lift-off, easier to hold angle.
goals.drag: Up: revs fall more between shifts. Down: revs stay up so the next gear pulls sooner.
goals.stability: Up: strong engine braking slows you when you lift. Down: the car coasts.

params.label: Flywheel weight
params.desc: How heavy the spinning engine is (kg·m²). The clutch divides spare torque by this to change rpm, so a light flywheel revs up and down very fast. It only matters while the clutch slips (launches, shifts, clutch kicks).
params.apply: live (read every step by the clutch)
params.risk: Below about 0.03 the rpm can jump hundreds of rpm per step and bounce off the limiter; never 0 (division by zero in the clutch, 0x29d460).

goals.launch: Up: rpm holds better when the clutch bites, less bog. Down: revs up fast but drops quickly off the line.
goals.drift: Up: clutch kicks feel lazy. Down: revs flare fast so clutch kicks hit hard.
goals.drag: Up: slower rev changes during shifts. Down: quicker rev matching on shifts.

params.label: Throttle curve
params.desc: The pedal is raised to this power before use (0.5 = square root). Lower numbers make a small pedal press give a lot of throttle. There is also a 10% dead zone after the curve.
params.apply: live. Note: the chassis Configure pass (0x27fe60, run when Driving Assist or DRIFT-PHYSICS is changed, and by any 'after' call to 0x27fe60) rewrites this field to its code default.
params.risk: Do not set 0 or negative (pow of 0 gives full throttle at any press).
params.source: 01-engine.md 2.3/2.6; read in throttle map 0x2869b4 (lwc1 0xec); written 0.5 by RaceCarEngine physics-mode 0x287bd0

goals.drift: Up: finer throttle control for holding angle with a pad. Down: small presses give big wheelspin.
goals.launch: Up: easier to feed throttle gently off the line. Down: touchy throttle that spins the tyres.

params.label: Torque multiplier
params.desc: Every value from the torque curve is multiplied by this. 1.2 means 20% more torque at every rpm. It does not change where the limiter is.
params.apply: live (also consider re-running the peak/band functions, see the torque-curve table)
params.risk: Very large torque can trigger the known wheel-spin hang (huge wheel accelerations) and overpower the 3x-peak-torque clutch cap.

goals.drag: Up: faster acceleration in every gear. Down: slower everywhere.
goals.launch: Up: more pull but more wheelspin off the line. Down: less wheelspin but slower.
goals.drift: Up: easier to keep the rear wheels spinning. Down: drifts die without wheelspin.
goals.highway: Up: higher top speed against drag. Down: lower top speed.

params.label: Torque multiplier 2
params.desc: A second torque multiplier used only by the race-car engine (ComputeTorque). It works like the first one.
params.apply: live. Note: the chassis Configure pass (0x27fe60, run when Driving Assist or DRIFT-PHYSICS is changed, and by any 'after' call to 0x27fe60) rewrites this field to its code default.
params.risk: Same as the first torque multiplier.

goals.drag: Up: faster acceleration. Down: slower.
goals.drift: Up: easier wheelspin. Down: harder to keep the rear spinning.

params.label: Rev limiter softness
params.desc: Above the last point of the torque curve, torque falls by half across this many rpm, and the engine can never go past max + this band. Bigger lets the engine over-rev further.
params.apply: live (copied into the working value 0xb8 every engine update, 0x2881b0)
params.risk: Never 0: TorqueAtRPM divides by the band (0x286af8 reads 0xb8).
params.source: 01-engine.md 2.3/2.6; read 0x2881b0 (lwc1 0xb4), copied to 0xb8 0x2881bc; 0xb8 read in TorqueAtRPM 0x286af8

goals.drag: Up: you can stay in a gear a bit longer past redline. Down: hard cut at redline.
goals.drift: Up: more room on the limiter mid-drift before you must shift. Down: you bounce off the limiter sooner.

params.label: Peak power for NOS cap
params.desc: The engine's peak horsepower, worked out once from the torque curve. NOS can add at most 200 / this value as a torque boost, so lowering it lets NOS add more. It also feeds the drift push force.
params.apply: live; recomputed by call 0x286568(engine) (that overwrites your edit)
params.risk: Never 0 (NOS divides 200 by it, 0x288794). Values far below the real peak make NOS huge.
params.source: 01-engine.md 2.3/2.6; read by NOS 0x288784 (lwc1 0xd0 via chassis+0x17c), written by Init 0x286500

goals.drag: Up: NOS boost is capped lower. Down: NOS can add more torque.

params.label: Peak torque for clutch cap
params.desc: Peak engine torque in lb-ft, worked out from the curve. The clutch can never carry more than 3 x this. Raising it lifts that ceiling.
params.risk: Very low values make the clutch slip all the time (car crawls).
params.source: 01-engine.md 2.3; clutch reads it 0x29d140 (lwc1 0xd4, cap = 3 x value); written by Init 0x286504

goals.launch: Up: the clutch can hold more torque. Down: clutch slips, softer launch.

params.label: NOS installed
params.desc: Turns the nitrous system on or off for this car. The NOS kit upgrade sets it to 1.
params.risk: With 0 litres left NOS still does nothing; set litres too.
params.source: 01-engine.md 2.3/2.4; written 0x2864e4 (default 0) and by the NOS keyword/upgrade

goals.drag: Up (on): you can use nitrous for a big boost. Down (off): no nitrous.
goals.highway: Up (on): nitrous helps reach top speed. Down (off): no boost.

params.label: NOS strength
params.desc: The NOS boost is (rpm / optimum rpm)² x this x the flow rate, capped at 200 hp worth. 1.0 is the normal kit.
params.risk: The 200 hp cap (code immediate 200.0 at 0x288788) still limits it; very high values just hit the cap sooner.

goals.drag: Up: NOS reaches its full boost at lower rpm. Down: weaker NOS.
goals.launch: Up: more NOS kick off the line. Down: less.

params.note: proof imm is relative to t1 = engine+0x80

params.label: NOS flow rate
params.desc: Litres of nitrous used each second. It also multiplies the boost, so a faster flow is stronger but runs out sooner.
params.risk: Huge values empty the bottle in one frame.

goals.drag: Up: stronger but shorter boost. Down: weaker but lasts longer.

params.note: proof imm is relative to t1 = engine+0x80

params.label: NOS best rpm
params.desc: NOS gives its full boost at or above this rpm and less below it (it scales with (rpm/this)²).

goals.drag: Up: NOS only strong near redline. Down: full NOS from lower rpm.
goals.launch: Up: weak NOS off the line. Down: strong NOS right away.

params.note: proof imm is relative to t1 = engine+0x80

params.label: NOS left
params.desc: How much nitrous is left in the bottle, in litres. It goes down while you hold the NOS button.

goals.drag: Up: more nitrous to use. Down: less.

params.note: proof imm is relative to t1 = engine+0x80

params.label: NOS bottle size
params.desc: The size of the nitrous bottle in litres (shown on the HUD). Refilling uses this.

goals.drag: Up: bigger bottle. Down: smaller bottle.

params.label: Clutch grip
params.desc: The most torque the clutch can pass (N·m), scaled by throttle: 10% at no throttle up to 100% at full. It is also capped at 3 x the engine's peak torque.
params.apply: live (0x74 holds a copy that is not used in the update)
params.risk: Very low values make the car crawl; 0 means no drive at all.

goals.launch: Up: the clutch bites hard and can bog or spin the tyres. Down: it slips, softer start.
goals.drag: Up: no clutch slip after shifts. Down: power is lost to slipping.
goals.drift: Up: clutch kicks hit harder. Down: kicks are soft.

params.label: Anti-stall speed
params.desc: Below this speed (m/s) the automatic clutch opens when the revs get low, so the engine does not stall, and keeps a little slip with no throttle.
params.source: 04-transmission.md auto clutch; read in forced-open rules 0x29c6f0 (lwc1 0xa0)

goals.launch: Up: clutch stays open longer at slow speed. Down: it closes sooner, sharper starts.

params.label: Launch control end speed
params.desc: The launch-control clutch helper stops at this speed (m/s), or when the clutch locks.

goals.launch: Up: launch helper manages the clutch for longer. Down: you get full clutch control sooner.

params.label: Final drive
params.desc: Every gear ratio is multiplied by this. A bigger number means faster acceleration but a lower top speed in each gear.
params.risk: Never 0 (speed maths divide by ratio x final).

goals.drag: Up: quicker acceleration, more shifts. Down: longer gears, slower pull.
goals.highway: Up: hits the limiter at a lower top speed. Down: higher top speed if the engine can pull it.
goals.launch: Up: more torque at the wheels off the line. Down: softer launch.
goals.drift: Up: easier wheelspin in low gears. Down: a gear holds a wider speed range.

params.label: Reverse gear
params.desc: The reverse gear ratio. The game stores it as a negative number; the editor shows it positive.

goals.stability: Up: stronger reverse. Down: gentler reverse.

params.label: Number of gears
params.desc: How many forward gears you can use. You can lower it to stop the box using top gears.
params.risk: Never set above the stock count unless you also fill the new ratios in the gear table: an empty (0) ratio divides by zero in the speed maths (0x298138) and can freeze the game. Max 13.

goals.highway: Up: more gears to reach top speed. Down: fewer gears, may cap top speed.

params.label: Upshift speed
params.desc: How much of an upshift happens each frame (1 / CHANGE-UP-TIME frames). 0.1 means 10 frames. During the shift the clutch is open and throttle is cut, so bigger is faster.
params.source: 04-transmission.md shifting; read 0x29890c (lwc1 0x80); copied to rate 0x7c on shift

goals.drag: Up: quicker upshifts, less time without power. Down: slow shifts lose speed.
goals.drift: Up: shifting mid-drift barely breaks traction. Down: long shifts can kill a drift.

params.label: Downshift speed
params.desc: How much of a downshift happens each frame (1 / CHANGE-DOWN-TIME frames).

goals.drift: Up: quick downshifts to set up a drift. Down: slow downshifts.
goals.grip: Up: faster corner entry downshifts. Down: slower.

params.label: Rev-match window
params.desc: If engine and wheel speeds are within this (shown in rpm) during a shift, the shift ends at once. Bigger means shifts finish sooner.
params.source: 04-transmission.md synchro; read 0x299a94 (lwc1 0x130); RX-7 CLUTCH-FACTOR 50 rad/s = 477 rpm

goals.drag: Up: shifts end early, less lost time. Down: full-length shifts.

params.label: Auto upshift rpm floor
params.desc: The automatic gearbox shifts up at the top of the 90%-power band, or at this rpm if it is higher. -1 means not used.
params.risk: Above the max rpm the auto box may never shift up.

goals.drag: Up: auto box holds gears to higher rpm. Down: it shifts at the power-band top.

params.label: Gearbox type
params.desc: The gearbox type picked in the menu: 1 auto, 2 semi-auto, 3 manual. The player code copies it into the active mode every frame.
params.source: 04-transmission.md modes; read by player code 0x2f7f5c (lw 0x74) then stored to 0x70

goals.drag: Up (manual): you pick shift points. Down (auto): the box shifts for you.
goals.drift: Up (manual): clutch kicks and held gears work. Down (auto): the box may shift mid-drift.

params.label: Gearbox drag (fixed)
params.desc: A fixed drag torque from the gearbox, applied to the driven axle while the car moves.

goals.highway: Up: a bit more drag, lower top speed. Down: less drag.

params.label: Diff lock (bias ratio)
params.desc: The slower wheel can get up to this many times the torque of the faster one. 1 = open diff, 10 = nearly locked. Upgrades reach 10.
params.apply: live (rear axle on RWD cars; skip axles whose vptr is not Torsen)

goals.drift: Up: both rear wheels spin together so the car slides and holds angle easily. Down: the inside wheel spins away and drifts fade.
goals.grip: Up: strong drive out of corners but more push-on understeer or snap. Down: smoother but the inside wheel spins.
goals.launch: Up: both wheels push off the line. Down: one wheel spins.
goals.stability: Up: power oversteer comes on sharper. Down: calmer on power.

params.label: Diff full-lock torque
params.desc: How much torque (plus preload) is needed before the full bias ratio is used. Lower means the diff locks fully with less throttle.
params.apply: live (rear axle on RWD cars; skip axles whose vptr is not Torsen)
params.risk: Division by these values happens (0x285e4c..), so never set full-lock torque or lock-in range to 0.

goals.drift: Up: needs lots of throttle to lock. Down: locks up even with a little throttle.
goals.grip: Up: gentle lock at part throttle. Down: locks hard early.

params.label: Diff preload
params.desc: Lock that is always there, even off throttle. If preload is equal to the full-lock torque the diff is always fully locked.
params.apply: live (rear axle on RWD cars; skip axles whose vptr is not Torsen)

goals.drift: Up: the diff stays locked off-throttle, drifts link easily. Down: the diff opens when you lift.
goals.stability: Up: the car pushes on corner entry. Down: free to turn when coasting.

params.label: Diff lock-in range
params.desc: The wheel speed difference over which the lock builds from nothing to full. Small means the diff locks as soon as the wheels differ.
params.apply: live (rear axle on RWD cars; skip axles whose vptr is not Torsen)
params.risk: Division by these values happens (0x285e4c..), so never set full-lock torque or lock-in range to 0.

goals.drift: Up: soft, progressive locking. Down: instant locking, sharper breakaway.

params.label: Diff coast lock
params.desc: How the diff acts off throttle (coasting). 1 or less: the faster wheel gets all the coast torque. Between 1 and 1.55: half lock. Above 1.55: full lock on coast.
params.apply: live (rear axle on RWD cars; skip axles whose vptr is not Torsen)

goals.drift: Up: coast lock keeps the car sliding when you lift. Down: lifting lets the rear grip up.
goals.stability: Up: lift-off can rotate the car. Down: lift-off is calm.

params.label: 4WD normal front share
params.desc: The share of torque sent to the front wheels when cruising (0 = all rear).
params.apply: live (only on cars with an i4WD block: Evo, WRX/STI, GT-R)
params.risk: Pointer is 0 on cars without i4WD: the editor must skip it. Division by the scales (0x285590..0x285604): never 0.
params.source: 05-differential.md 3.4; RaceCarI4wdController::Update 0x285588; i4WD pointer stored at clutch+0x94 by Bind 0x29c51c

goals.drift: Up: more front pull, harder to slide. Down: rear-biased, easier to drift.
goals.grip: Up: more front drive, stable exits. Down: more rear steer.
goals.launch: Up: more wheels pushing off the line. Down: rear wheelspin.

params.label: 4WD drift front share
params.desc: The most torque sent forward when the car detects a slide, to pull it straight. Also used below 20 m/s.
params.apply: live (only on cars with an i4WD block: Evo, WRX/STI, GT-R)
params.risk: Pointer is 0 on cars without i4WD: the editor must skip it. Division by the scales (0x285590..0x285604): never 0.
params.source: 05-differential.md 3.4; RaceCarI4wdController::Update 0x285588; i4WD pointer stored at clutch+0x94 by Bind 0x29c51c

goals.drift: Up: the car pulls itself out of drifts. Down: lets the slide go on.
goals.stability: Up: strong anti-spin pull. Down: less help.
goals.launch: Up: more front drive at low speed. Down: rear-heavy launches.

params.label: 4WD transfer smoothness
params.desc: Above 0 the front share changes smoothly with how far past the drift limit you are; 0 or less makes it jump between normal and drift share.
params.apply: live (only on cars with an i4WD block: Evo, WRX/STI, GT-R)
params.risk: Pointer is 0 on cars without i4WD: the editor must skip it. Division by the scales (0x285590..0x285604): never 0.
params.source: 05-differential.md 3.4; RaceCarI4wdController::Update 0x285588; i4WD pointer stored at clutch+0x94 by Bind 0x29c51c

goals.drift: Up: smooth, early shifting of torque forward. Down: on/off switching.

params.label: 4WD drift angle scale
params.desc: Rear slip (rad) used to judge a drift; bigger lets more angle happen before torque moves forward.
params.apply: live (only on cars with an i4WD block: Evo, WRX/STI, GT-R)
params.risk: Pointer is 0 on cars without i4WD: the editor must skip it. Division by the scales (0x285590..0x285604): never 0.
params.source: 05-differential.md 3.4; RaceCarI4wdController::Update 0x285588; i4WD pointer stored at clutch+0x94 by Bind 0x29c51c

goals.drift: Up: more angle before the 4WD steps in. Down: it steps in early.

params.label: 4WD drift yaw scale
params.desc: Allowed turning speed (rad/s) before the 4WD calls it a drift; bigger allows faster rotation.
params.apply: live (only on cars with an i4WD block: Evo, WRX/STI, GT-R)
params.risk: Pointer is 0 on cars without i4WD: the editor must skip it. Division by the scales (0x285590..0x285604): never 0.
params.source: 05-differential.md 3.4; RaceCarI4wdController::Update 0x285588; i4WD pointer stored at clutch+0x94 by Bind 0x29c51c

goals.drift: Up: more rotation allowed. Down: pulls straight quickly.
goals.stability: Up: less anti-spin help. Down: more help.

params.label: Spring rate
params.desc: How stiff each spring is (N/m, per wheel). Stiff springs move less, so the body rolls and dives less but bumps hit harder. The damper strength also scales with it.
params.apply: live; then run the after call so static sag and per-wheel mass are recomputed
params.risk: Very soft springs plus big loads can bottom out every step; extreme stiffness with landings is limited only by the 40 x mass force clamp. Do not set 0 (damping uses sqrt(k x m) and sag divides by k, 0x279328).

goals.grip: Up: sharper turn-in and less roll. Down: more grip on bumpy roads.
goals.drift: Up (front): quicker direction changes for linking. Down (rear): more rear grip, harder to slide.
goals.stability: Up: jumpy over bumps and landings. Down: soaks up bumps.
goals.highway: Up: steadier at speed with downforce. Down: floaty at high speed.

params.label: Bump damping
params.desc: How much the shock slows the wheel going up. The game stores the square root of this ratio; damper force = 2·sqrt(k·m)·sqrt(ratio)·speed.
params.apply: live (raw ratio also kept at 0x13c, not read)
params.risk: Very high values plus a landing make huge force spikes (cut only by the 40 x mass clamp).

goals.grip: Up: quicker weight transfer, sharper response. Down: lazier.
goals.stability: Up: harsh over bumps. Down: wallowy, bouncy.
goals.drift: Up: snappier transitions. Down: smoother transitions.

params.label: Rebound damping
params.desc: How much the shock slows the wheel coming back down. Stored as the square root of the ratio.
params.apply: live (raw ratio also kept at 0x144, not read)
params.risk: Very high values keep the wheel off the ground after bumps (less grip).

goals.stability: Up: body settles fast after bumps. Down: bouncy.
goals.grip: Up: controlled body until the wheels start to skip. Down: the body floats and grip comes and goes.

params.label: Ride height
params.desc: How high the wheel hangs below the body mount (m). The game added the static sag (+0.01 m) to the script value once at load, so the live number is about 0.05 m bigger than the script.
params.apply: poke, then call 0x273480(car, axle) to move the wheel mounts
params.risk: Only re-placing the mounts (after) makes it take effect. Very low values bottom the body on the ground.
params.source: 02-suspension.md 5; read by wheel placement 0x27334c (lwc1 0x14c); stock_example is the script value (live ≈ +0.045 sag +0.01)

goals.stability: Up: more room over bumps and jumps. Down: hits the ground.
goals.grip: Up: body sits high, more roll. Down: lower and flatter.

params.label: Downforce
params.desc: Push-down force per axle: DOWNFORCE x speed² / (distance from axle to centre of mass). It is a real force pushing the body into the springs.
params.risk: Huge values crush the springs at speed (bottoming).

goals.highway: Up: steadier and more grip at high speed. Down: lighter and twitchy at speed.
goals.grip: Up: more grip in fast corners. Down: less.
goals.drift: Up (rear): rear sticks at speed, harder to slide. Down (rear): looser at speed.

params.label: Axle drive share
params.desc: How much engine torque this axle gets (0 = none). Torque per axle = torque / sum of shares x this share. Giving the front axle 1 on a RWD car makes it 50/50 AWD (open front diff).
params.apply: live (also poke 0x170 to survive a reset; i4WD cars rewrite it every frame)

goals.drift: Up (rear): classic RWD slides. Down (rear, with front up): the car pulls straight.
goals.launch: Up (both): AWD launch. Down: one axle spins.
goals.grip: Up (front): stable exits. Down (front): more rotation.

params.label: Axle brake share
params.desc: 1 means this axle gets brakes, 0 means no brakes on this axle (BRAKE-TORQUE-ENABLED / BIAS).

goals.stability: Up: this axle helps stop. Down: no braking here.

params.label: Axle roll stiffness
params.desc: A simple roll bar built into the axle (ROLL-BAR-STIFFNESS); pushes the wheels together in roll. No disc car uses it (0).

goals.grip: Up: less roll, quicker response. Down: more grip on uneven ground.
goals.drift: Up (rear): looser rear. Down (rear): more rear grip.

params.label: Anti-roll geometry
params.desc: Fraction of the roll moment turned straight into wheel load (like real suspension geometry). 0 on race cars.

goals.grip: Up: less body roll. Down: more roll.
goals.stability: Up: flatter body. Down: more lean.

params.label: Anti-pitch geometry
params.desc: Fraction of the dive/squat moment turned straight into wheel load. 0 on race cars.

goals.launch: Up: less squat on launch. Down: more squat.
goals.stability: Up: less dive when braking. Down: more dive.

params.label: Wheel draw limit
params.desc: How far up the wheel is drawn (visual only, m above sag). It does not change the physics.

goals.stability: Up: wheels drawn higher, no handling change. Down: wheels drawn lower, no handling change.

params.label: Camber
params.desc: Static wheel tilt (shown in degrees, stored in radians). The tyre maths uses camber in the lateral force (PDY3 reduces grip with camber², PHY3/PVY3 shift it).

goals.grip: Up (toward 0): less camber thrust. Down (more negative): more thrust until PDY3 cuts grip.
goals.drift: Up (rear toward 0): rear grips less. Down (more negative): rear holds.

params.label: Toe
params.desc: Static toe angle (degrees shown, radians stored), mirrored left/right. Added to the wheel angle every step.
params.risk: Big values scrub speed and heat nothing (no heat model) but slow the car.

goals.stability: Up (toe-in, rear): steadier straight line. Down (toe-out): twitchy.
goals.grip: Up (front toe-in): lazier turn-in. Down (toe-out): sharper turn-in.
goals.highway: Up (a little toe-in): stable at speed. Down (toe-out): wanders.

params.label: Anti-roll bar (front)
params.desc: Front roll bar strength (N/m). Force = k x (left travel - right travel), max 0.7 x k, moved between the two front tyres.
params.apply: live (check +0x70 == 1 for FRONT, 2 for REAR before writing)

goals.grip: Up: less roll but the front loses grip sooner (understeer). Down: more front grip.
goals.drift: Up: the front washes out and the car resists rotating. Down: the front bites so the car turns into slides.
goals.stability: Up: flatter, calmer body. Down: leans more.

params.label: Anti-roll bar (rear)
params.desc: Rear roll bar strength. A stiffer rear bar takes grip away from the rear in corners. The RX-7 TRS has no rear bar (component absent).
params.apply: live (only if the car has a REAR bar; +0x70 == 2)
params.risk: Missing on 25 cars (front only): the editor must skip it.

goals.drift: Up: rear lets go more easily, easier to drift. Down: rear grips.
goals.grip: Up: more rotation. Down: more rear grip.
goals.stability: Up: tail-happy. Down: planted rear.

tables.label: Torque curve
tables.desc: Engine torque (N·m) at each rpm; the game draws straight lines between points. The first point is idle rpm and the last is max rpm. Raising a point gives more pull at that rpm.
tables.apply: live for torque; then run the after calls: 0x286568(engine) recomputes peak hp/torque of the working curve (0xd0/0xd4: NOS cap, clutch cap); the stock peaks 0xd8..0xe4 are only read by the upgrade reshape at car init (0x287680) and need no recompute and 0x288a30(engine) rebuilds the 10 power bands at 0x158 (auto upshift rpm, launch-control target, good-shift window). The stock copy is a second Table2d at engine+0x1d0 (same layout) for reset. Point count is fixed (no realloc): edit existing points only.
tables.risk: rpm values must keep increasing (the lookup is a binary search). Moving the last rpm changes the limiter. Huge torque can trigger the wheel-spin hang.
tables.source: 01-engine.md 2.1; Table2d first x 0x146d08 (lw 0(a0)), last x 0x146d18 (lw 4(a0) count); band builder 0x288a30 uses engine+0xa0

goals.drift: Up at mid rpm: easier to keep wheels spinning mid-drift. Down: drifts bog.
goals.highway: Up near redline: more top speed. Down: less.

tables.label: Gear ratios
tables.desc: Forward gear ratios, 1st first. The wheel torque is engine torque x gear x final drive. Reverse is stored separately (negated, gearbox+0xec) and the final drive at +0xf0; neutral is 0.
tables.risk: No ratio may be 0 (road-speed maths divide by ratio x final). Array holds 13 slots; the count field 0xb0 says how many are used.

goals.launch: Up (1st): harder launch, more wheelspin. Down (1st): softer launch.

tables.label: Pacejka coefficients
tables.desc: The 47 Magic Formula numbers of the tyre (MF 5.x names). PDX1 = forward peak grip, PDY1 = side peak grip (negative), PKY1 = cornering stiffness (negative), PCY1/PEY1 = shape of the side-force curve past the peak, RBX1/RBY1 = how slip in one direction cuts grip in the other. The fast path ignores PEX4, PVX1/2, RBX2, RHX1, RHY1, RVY1..6.
tables.apply: live, but cached B/C/D/E only refresh when load moves 50 N or camber changes: poke 0 into tyre{a}{w}+0xe8 for each of the 4 tyres (one-shot), or set tyredata+0x58c = 1 (refresh every step). Then rebuild the peak-slip tables (used by the slip limiter and the steering lock) with after: 0x28fab8(tyredata) - a heavy one-shot that builds a temporary tyre, sets and clears 0x58c itself.
tables.risk: The tyre model object is shared by every wheel (and every car) that uses the same WHEEL name: on the RX-7 TRS all four wheels use "97RX7TRSR-FRONT", so one edit changes all four, and also AI cars of the same model. 0x28fab8 runs 101 loads x ~150 force evaluations: call it once per edit, not per frame (believed safe: self-contained alloc/free; not run-tested while driving). Setting PVX1/PVX2/RBX2/PEX4/RHY1/RVY1-4/RVY6 non-zero does NOT switch to the full path (mode is chosen at parse). PDY1 must stay negative and PDX1 positive. Dividing terms: Bx = Kx/(Cx·Dx), By = Ky/(Cy·Dy): PCX1, PCY1, PDX1, PDY1 must never be 0.
tables.source: 03-tyre.md 2.4; fast path 0x28ce20: base s1 = model+0x594 (0x28ce40); PCX1 0x28cfc4 (+0), PDX1 0x28cfa8 (+4), PHX1 0x28cf94 (+0x28), PKX1 0x28d008 (+0x1c)

goals.grip: Up |PDY1|: more cornering grip. Down: less.
goals.drift: Up (sharper drop past the peak via PCY1/PEY1): snappy slides. Down (flatter): slides stay controllable.
goals.launch: Up PDX1: more traction. Down: wheelspin.
goals.stability: Up |PKY1|: sharper, more nervous response. Down: lazier but forgiving.

tables.label: Suspension kinematics polynomial
tables.desc: How the wheel moves as the suspension compresses: for travel u (from static sag), each channel = sum of row[k] x u^k. Channels: track change (m), wheelbase change (m), camber change and toe (bump steer). Front RX-7: -45° camber and -33° toe per metre of bump.
tables.apply: live (only used when DATA-TYPE is POLYNOMIAL, kin+0x74 == 1). Row 0 = constant, row 1 = linear, ... (max 4 rows).
tables.risk: Big toe terms make the car dart over bumps. Count must stay <= 4 (jump table 0x565a80).

goals.grip: Up (more camber gain in row 1): the loaded tyre stays flatter in roll. Down: less camber gain.
goals.stability: Up (more bump-steer in row 1 toe): darty over bumps. Down (toe toward 0): steadier over bumps.
goals.drift: Up (rear toe-in gain): rear steers itself straight under squat. Down: rear steers out, looser.
